of related to garbage collections in AOT cache. So, the AOT cache stores Java heap objects in a GC or garbage collector specific but also heap layout compatible format.
Uh this is what is allowing the JVM to memory map those cached objects directly into the heap for fast startup. So, that's pretty much the secret sauce of making

it fast. However, garbage collectors, they represent object references differently. So, each of the G1 versus ZGC, for example, they are representing the references differently. They are like compressed

versus uncompressed pointers. And depending on the heap size and region, could be different placement rules of those references. So, because of these disparities, for a long time when I was giving the

garbage collector. But that now I can fully say that's no longer the case because these incompatible reference formats has been solved in JDK 26
and has been ported to the Oracle JDK as well, and I expect that other vendors have done the same, hopefully. Um so, these incompatibilities are not there
anymore. Uh so, now there are two flags that can help you to instruct an AOT uh cache creation and how to have how for garbage collection should handle the
objects. So, if you're using the GC specific the mappable objects, the pretty much that one, well, you can get a nearly instant warm-up start and
because the cache is likely already in the file system. Now, the GC agnostic the streamable version can hide this latency on cold start. So,
that's all something that you should know. My advice is actually to prefer the streamable GC agnostic if training with ZGC. So, if you know that you're a ZGC
user. And there are some conditions for that. You can if that is being done there training with GDC or if you're using the use compressed ops option or your heap
